findings.claim: In execReviewStatus, exec.LookPath(gentleAIBinary) runs at line 164 before the bounded context (context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), statusExecTimeout)) is created at line 174, so PATH resolution for the gentle-ai binary is not covered by the statusExecTimeout/statusWaitDelay deadline machinery this same function documents as existing specifically to keep the guard from hanging. exec.LookPath performs an os.Stat call per PATH directory with no deadline parameter of its own, so a PATH entry that blocks on stat (e.g. an unresponsive network-mounted or stale-automount directory) hangs review-preflight indefinitely before any timeout is even armed, contradicting the function's own stated latency guarantee ('a guard that can hang indefinitely is one operators learn to skip').

findings.claim: cmd_review_preflight's exit-code remap treats 'CALLER_CWD no longer exists' as the only reason `cd "$CALLER_CWD"` can fail. If that cd instead fails for a different reason while the path still stats as a directory (e.g. permission denied, a stale/unmounted bind mount), the guard binary is never actually invoked, yet status stays at the cd failure's own code (typically 1) because `! -d "$CALLER_CWD"` is false — which this guard's own exit-code contract reads as outcomeEmptyCandidate (1, a specific verdict) rather than outcomeUndetermined (3, no verdict reached), the exact absence-of-proof-read-as-a-verdict failure mode this feature exists to prevent.
proof_refs: bin/labdrian-overlay:1699-1700 `(cd "$CALLER_CWD" && "$guard_binary" "$@") || status=$?`

bin/labdrian-overlay:1701-1706 comment and remap scope the fix explicitly to 'A CALLER_CWD that no longer exists', and the guard condition is only `[[ "$status" -ne 0 && ! -d "$CALLER_CWD" ]]`, which is false whenever the path still exists as a directory regardless of why cd failed

tools/review-preflight/main.go's outcomeEmptyCandidate=1 vs outcomeUndetermined=3 constants (and their surrounding doc comment) are deliberately distinct verdicts — 'Only outcomeCovered asserts that starting a review here is safe... A guard that guessed "probably fine" when it could not read the projection would reproduce that failure one layer up' — the same design intent this narrower bash remap does not fully honor for non-existence-unrelated cd failures

findings.claim: cmd_review_preflight's exit-code remap treats 'CALLER_CWD no longer exists' as the only reason `cd "$CALLER_CWD"` can fail. If that cd instead fails for a different reason while the path still stats as a directory (e.g. permission denied, a stale/unmounted bind mount), the guard binary is never actually invoked, yet status stays at the cd failure's own code (typically 1) because `! -d "$CALLER_CWD"` is false — which this guard's own exit-code contract reads as outcomeEmptyCandidate (1, a specific verdict) rather than outcomeUndetermined (3, no verdict reached), the exact absence-of-proof-read-as-a-verdict failure mode this feature exists to prevent.
proof_refs: bin/labdrian-overlay:1699-1700 `(cd "$CALLER_CWD" && "$guard_binary" "$@") || status=$?`

bin/labdrian-overlay:1701-1706 comment and remap scope the fix explicitly to 'A CALLER_CWD that no longer exists', and the guard condition is only `[[ "$status" -ne 0 && ! -d "$CALLER_CWD" ]]`, which is false whenever the path still exists as a directory regardless of why cd failed

tools/review-preflight/main.go's outcomeEmptyCandidate=1 vs outcomeUndetermined=3 constants (and their surrounding doc comment) are deliberately distinct verdicts — 'Only outcomeCovered asserts that starting a review here is safe... A guard that guessed "probably fine" when it could not read the projection would reproduce that failure one layer up' — the same design intent this narrower bash remap does not fully honor for non-existence-unrelated cd failures
